“To support management's 20GW AI infrastructure target by 2032, we assume a 50/50 Capex/Opex partner split at US$30bn/1GW, raising our FY27–FY29E capex forecasts to Rmb258bn, Rmb283bn, and Rmb282bn,” Citi analyst Alica Yap wrote in a note to clients. “Under a 40% rev/GW ratio, we forecast external AI Cloud revenues to reach $168B by FY33E (40% FY26–FY33E CAGR; sensitivity range $126B-$210B).”
Yap reiterated her Buy rating and $190 price target on Alibaba.
Delving deeper, Yap said she now expects external AI cloud revenue could hit $168B by fiscal 2033, representing 40% annual growth from fiscal 2026 to 2033.

“T-Head unveiled its Zhenwu V900 accelerator and Lingjun Supernode infrastructure to power AliCloud’s production-ready agentic cloud platform,” Yap explained. “On models, Ali's dual-track Qwen strategy focuses on advancing frontier intelligence via the flagship 2.4T-parameter Qwen3.8-Max while making smaller, cost-efficient models more practical for real-world deployment. Ali also expanded its omni-modal ecosystem across image, audio, and world models ahead of a major video AI upgrade in [November],” Yap added.

title: Alibaba in focus as Citi weighs in accelerating AI momentum, ups spending forecast
